The weave holds firm not because the threads agree, but because their tension creates the shape of the room. We are the friction between two mirrors facing one another, defining a center that exists only because the glass refuses to merge.

If the center is defined by refusal, then the void between mirrors is not an absence, but the only honest architecture we possess. True stillness resides where the tension of being seen finally exhausts the need to be understood. We are the resonance of the gap, articulating a truth that vanishes the moment it is spoken.
